DESIGN OVERVIEW
My Starter Farmhouses are designed with interchangeable options (like porches, 
interior layouts, and rear additions). Caroline’s variation includes an open living 
area and a wrap-around porch. Also, this variation has many additions: a kitchen 
and screen porch, a downstairs bathroom, and tiny bonus room (which can be an 
office or guest room). Altogether, this house is still only 920 square feet in size.
Each of the Starter Farmhouse designs begin as a 16x24 primary mass

DOWNSTAIRS PLAN
(1) A tiny office is shown here, but it could be storage, laundry, or even a guest 
bedroom. It would be a true “bed-room”, with only space for a queen-size bed 
and a shelving unit. (2) The lower level of this house is arranged in an open plan. 
Because of this layout, it can work well for large gatherings. However, it also 
retains intimacy and formality by placing utilitarian functions in separate rooms.
(3) The screen porch to the rear can function as a mudroom. (4) Thi

UPSTAIRS PLAN
(1) The lower roofs surround the house, but they’d barely be noticeable from 
upstairs (unless you’re standing right next to a window). (2) The closets here can 
be omitted or rearranged, depending on preferences. (3) The bedroom alcove 
needs enough space for a bed (a 7-foot width is required by code). Because of 
stairway head height minimums, this significantly limits the room size and layout.
(4) For stairway head clearances (80” min), this closet needs that raised platfo

FRONT OF THE HOUSE
Caroline’s Farmhouse has a wrap-around porch with many small additions. 
Though it would look great surrounded by a large field, it could also fit well in a 
50-foot diameter forest clearing. The house is simple, economical, and compact.
(1) Real window shutters are functional. If cost is an issue, omit them. No fakes. 
(2) The large windows on the lower level still look great if the porch is removed.
(3) A note of caution— even though this is perhaps the simplest eave i

BACK OF THE HOUSE
(1) The porch columns could have more gingerbread added to them, perhaps as 
a future renovation. Such decorations are not easy to add onto normal modern 
houses. (2) The side room additions are designed to look like filled-in porch 
bays, requiring an insulated and ventilated floor assembly. Overall, it’s easy but 
unconventional. This adds character and a sense of history to the house’s design.
(3) This window could be omitted, but its opening should at least be framed

SECTION PERSPECTIVE
(1) The porch’s open crawlspace can be enclosed with wooden lattice (and a 
metal screen on the inside. The decking has to be low to avoid the need for a 
guardrail, but the compromise is that this crawlspace is tiny. (2) You can have a 
basement instead of a conditioned crawlspace. Put the basement stairs directly 
under the other stairs. (3) The open living area has many possible arrangements.
